items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And I finally got two string basses in the band. Jimmy Johnson and Harold Holmes.

ctx.x: Yeah. All planned in the front. Right. Well, what about somebody like Jimmy Johnson? He couldn't have been young. The bass player? The bass player.
No, Jimmy was an old man.
But was he in shape enough to travel?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: The last job he played with me was in Mobile, Alabama.

ctx.x: This is June the 6th, 1961, and I'm Paul Crawford. You were talking about this fellow, one of the first guys you took, you know, when you left New Orleans? No. A banjo player or something?

Yes, I remember that real well. And right here's a picture of him, Paul. Richard McCarthy. I was 16 years old, and Richard I think was 17 or 18. We were in the same bracket there. And then we also had another fellow just a little older, maybe about six or seven months. His name was Johnson. What did he play? He was the alto player. Uh-huh. That was the three that I took out of New Orleans that year going to Dallas.
Did you have a job when you left New Orleans or what were you doing?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: I had Jimmy Johnson on the string bass.

ctx.x: So you got a real close song, didn't you?

That was the first bass song. And then when we went up a little further, when we added Geechee Robinson, another drum roll. We had Nick Turner, another bass record. I had Jimmy Johnson on the string bass. And I had Nick Turner on the Suze for MWM on the drum roll. And then later on I added Harold Holmes, who's now in Canada, who did most of my arranging. And as we traveled over the country, I added here, subtracted, added and subtracted.
And I found the change in the years. Did you ever play any other state fairs? You want to start it by now or is it?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: I had one of the musicians in my band as a product of those old bands, one of my first bands, that was old Jimmy Johnson.

ctx.x: Well, I imagine he was busy with his band.

Always busy. Always busy. And I had one of the musicians in my band as a product of those old bands, one of my first bands, that was old Jimmy Johnson. See, Jimmy played with Buddy Bowling and those guys.
Did he read much or was he fake?
